title: The Flight of the Phoenix
full_review:
"The Flight of the Phoenix" (20th Century Fox) is an underwhelming remake of the 1966 James Stewart action adventure about a cargo plane full of recently evacuated oil-rig workers which crashes off-course in a remote region of the Gobi desert, leaving the survivors -- including the gruff and macho pilot (Dennis Quaid, in the Stewart role), a plucky and pretty geologist (Miranda Otto) and a towheaded mystery man (a bleached blond Giovanni Ribisi) -- without a radio and with dwindling rations.

With hope of rescue fading, the castaways decide to build a makeshift plane from the downed wreckage, christening it after the mythic bird that rose out of its own ashes.

In addition to the usual internecine frictions and personality clashes, the rag-tag bunch must also contend with killer sandstorms and hostile Mongolian marauders.

Neither Quaid nor Ribisi can hold a candle to Stewart or Hardy Kruger, and a supporting cast which includes Tyrese Gibson, Tony Curran, rap-artist Sticky Fingaz and Jacob Vargas is a far cry from Ernest Borgnine, George Kennedy, Richard Attenborough and Peter Finch.

Still, while the setting has been changed from the Sahara to the Gobi and the ensemble is more ethnically diverse, the remake pretty much follows the original's lead. The 1966 version was directed by Robert Aldrich, who would go on to direct "The Dirty Dozen."

The new film, produced by Aldrich's son, William, and directed by John Moore, boasts some nice desert photography and manages to take off in the final half-hour, but most of this "Flight" is grounded by bland performances (Ribisi excluded), corny dialogue and an undernourished script.

The film contains some violence, including a murder and an intense plane crash, an anti-religious comment and intermittent crude language. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-III -- adults. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG-13 -- parents are strongly cautioned. Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.
